date_note: Newsway (23 November) says the Financial Services Commission voted the fine at its regular meeting that day.
exec: A Korean regulator fined a card issuer for telling bond investors no data-leak risk was confirmed while a hacking incident was under way.
geo_basis: agency: Financial Services Commission, Seoul; the source gives no other location
plain: South Korea's financial regulator fined Lotte Card for not properly warning bond investors about the risk from a 2025 hacking incident that leaked customers' personal data.

evidence.quote: 금융위원회는 이날 정례회의를 열고 롯데카드의 자본시장법상 공시의무 위반에 대해 약 10억 2000만원의 과징금 부과를 의결했다.
해당 해킹 사고로 개인정보가 유출된 고객은 약 297만명에 달한다.

summary: South Korea's Financial Services Commission voted on 23 November to fine Lotte Card 약 10억 2000만원 for breaching Capital Markets Act disclosure duties, Newsway reports. Its 16 September 2025 bond filing said no personal-data leak risk had been confirmed, while a hacking incident was under investigation; Newsway puts the customers whose data leaked at 약 297만명 (roughly a third of all customers). Lotte Card says it disclosed before the leak was confirmed.
title: Korea's Financial Services Commission fines Lotte Card over hacking-risk disclosure in a bond filing

validation.note: Newsway read in full; it reports the Financial Services Commission's decision. The commission's own release was not found; a search found only earlier coverage of the prior notice (SBS Biz).
